relationships.subject: RONS
relationships.evidence_quote: RONS may activate TRPA1, which induces CGRP release, contributing to migraine.

relationships.subject: TRPA1
relationships.evidence_quote: TRPA1 activation by its agonists may lead to the release of neuropeptides, including CGRP and substance P, which are crucial in migraine pathogenesis

relationships.subject: MAPK1/2
relationships.evidence_quote: The increased expression of CGRP induced by TRPA1 activation was inhibited by a selective inhibitor of mitogen-activated protein kinase 1/2 (MAPK1/2) in dorsal root ganglion neurons

relationships.subject: TRPV1
relationships.evidence_quote: The production of RONS in meningeal nociceptors can be triggered by the activation of transient receptor potential cation channel subfamily V member 1 (TRPV1)

key_findings: Review proposes RONS-TRPA1-CGRP axis, with epigenetic modification of its components, as a driver of migraine pathophysiology.
Only non-coding RNAs are currently considered feasible to target the axis epigenetically.
